title: Purpose, Money Mindset & Behavioral Finance
intro: This opening section frames money as a system of behavior, identity, incentives, and choices. The infographics connect practical personal finance to the mental models behind wealth: patience, discipline, simplicity, emotional control, and values-driven decision-making. It is the foundation for the rest of The Money Map because the best financial plan is only useful when it matches how people actually think, feel, and act.

title: Cash Flow, Savings, Net Worth & Wealth Stages
intro: Wealth begins with the gap between income and spending, then compounds through consistent saving, intentional budgeting, and measurable net worth progress. This section organizes the core mechanics of household finance: savings rates, emergency capacity, spending categories, age-band benchmarks, compounding, and the wealth ladder from earned income to financial freedom.

title: Debt, Credit & Financial Safety
intro: A strong financial life requires defense as much as offense. These maps focus on the systems that protect cash flow and optionality: emergency funds, credit health, debt payoff order, and resilience against life disruptions. The goal is not just to eliminate bad debt, but to build a stable base that makes every other financial decision easier.

title: Investing, Markets & Portfolio Strategy
intro: This section moves from saving money to deploying capital. The infographics cover allocation, diversification, rebalancing, market cycles, stock indicators, taxable investing choices, and disciplined selling. Together, they translate investing from a guessing game into a repeatable process built around risk, time horizon, valuation, and behavior.

title: Taxes, Capital Gains & Account Buckets
intro: Taxes shape the real return of every financial decision. These maps simplify tax brackets, account types, capital gains, retirement withdrawal taxation, marital tax differences, and the three major investing buckets. The practical emphasis is on sequencing, location, timing, and using the tax code intentionally rather than reactively.

lessons.title: Tax Differences for Single vs. Married Households

title: Retirement, FIRE & Benefits
intro: Retirement planning is a timeline, not a single number. This section brings together withdrawal rates, account access rules, Social Security, workplace benefits, FIRE progress, retirement accounts, and single-versus-couple planning. The maps show how financial independence depends on savings rate, benefits strategy, taxes, healthcare, and flexible withdrawal design.

title: Insurance, Healthcare & Protection Planning
intro: Risk protection is one of the least glamorous but most important parts of wealth building. These infographics explain insurance layers, health plan trade-offs, Medicare versus Medicaid versus private insurance, and healthcare planning by life stage. The purpose is to help households protect their downside before pursuing higher-risk upside.

title: Housing & Real Estate
intro: Housing is often the largest line item, largest asset, and largest emotional purchase in a household budget. This section maps the cash-to-close process, affordability, and real estate decision rules. The focus is on understanding total cost, leverage, interest rates, reserves, and the difference between buying a home and making a good financial decision.

title: Family, Couples, Kids & College Planning
intro: Money becomes more complex when households grow, combine, or plan for children. These maps cover shared expenses, marriage versus single finances, family wealth systems, college funding, 529 plans, child-rearing costs, and education ROI. The section is designed to make family financial planning less reactive and more intentional.

lessons.title: The College Map: Top 100 U.S. Colleges and How to Pay for Them

title: Income, Entrepreneurship & Alternative Assets
intro: The Money Map also treats wealth as an entrepreneurial system. This section explores income streams, side hustles, retail arbitrage, family and self-driven earning power, collectibles, and alternative assets. The common theme is optionality: expanding what can produce income or store value while understanding liquidity, concentration, and risk.

lessons.title: Top Income Streams for Anyone in Life

title: Life Morality, Meaning & Legacy
intro: The final section zooms out from tactics to meaning. These infographics explore life lessons, regrets, legacy, FIRE morals, dying with zero, estate planning, and the balance between money, health, relationships, and happiness. The purpose is to remind readers that wealth is a tool, and the highest return is a life lived with purpose, stewardship, and fewer regrets.
